candidates.summary: Nolan Lawson benchmarked 12 JavaScript frameworks by having Opus 5.5 build the same small Pokémon app five times in each, then measuring cost, lines of code, Lighthouse scores and JavaScript shipped, to test 'better for agents' claims with evidence.
facts: Setup: same spec given to Opus 5.5 (high effort) in a sandbox, each framework's official MCP or skills installed, output tested against a conformance suite based on the accessibility tree; median of 5 runs (3 for Angular, which twice failed to produce a measurable app).
Median API-priced cost per build ranged from $2.67 (Hono+htmx), $2.76 (Astro) and $2.82 (Nuxt) up to $4.28 (SvelteKit), $4.65 (Gracile+Lit) and $4.97 (Angular); Next.js was $3.14.
Median lines of code ranged from 1,370 (Hono+htmx) to 2,009 (Angular).
Lighthouse performance and accessibility were near-saturated for all frameworks (performance 97 to 100, accessibility 100); JavaScript shipped ranged from 0 KiB (Astro) to 93 KiB (Angular).

Agents often ignored installed tooling: the Nuxt MCP was never used, and Next.js agents read the skill file in 1 of 5 runs. Lawson: 'I have a strong suspicion, for example, that the current crop of MCPs and skills may be doing more harm than good.'
The benchmark is on GitHub for others to rerun; Hacker News thread reached 277 points.

source.name: Nolan Lawson: The AI cost of JavaScript frameworks

candidates.summary: DeepSeek open-sourced dsh-superagent, an MIT-licensed research prototype of a proactive coding agent that watches one GitHub repository (and optionally Feishu), takes work from allowed people, does it in its own isolated session and answers with results such as a pull request.
facts: README: 'Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product'; much of the engineering was done by coding agents, and it differs from DeepSeek's internal version.
It is packaged as a bundle for DeepSeek Harness; a web panel shows what needs a person.
Stated principle: 'take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible'; it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it.
Setup is done by asking your coding agent to read SETUP.md and set it up with you.
Repo created Oct 31, 2026; 7,155 GitHub stars at capture.

candidates.summary: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch posted 'Own your intelligence', arguing that local models need to keep proliferating and that builders should own their harness, data, connections and runtime rather than rent them.
facts: Post: 'Own your intelligence. Anyone that opposes this has something to sell you (perhaps your own intelligence back to you.)'
Post: 'Own your harness, data, connections, runtime: your agents. Embrace open source.'
He notes the largest models 'may be out of reach for now locally', so the best option is to keep options open.
